learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri S.P. Pandey, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
2. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.205 of 2024, under Sections 363, 376 (2)n I.P.C. and Section 5L/6 POCSO Act, Police Station C.B. Ganj, District Bareilly, during the pendency of trial.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant is stated to have sexually molested the victim for about three years, who happens to be the daughter of the informant, and he is stated to have enticed her away on 12.06.2024.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
4. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
5. The FIR is delayed by one day and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
6. The victim, by her looks, seems to be major although as per Class-Xth certificate, her date of birth is 18.07.2007, as such her age comes out to be 16 years, 10 months and 25 days.
7.
The victim has not whispered a single word against the applicant in the FIR regarding she being enticed away by the applicant.
She has stated that fearing the backlash, she had left her house and gone on her own to Kasganj by train.

On hearing the news of illness of her father, she returned to her house, although she has mentioned that the applicant used to sexually assault her and he had taken Rs.80,000/- from her alongwith ATM card of her grand-father.
8. The allegations regarding giving Rs.80,000/- to the applicant are false and is not substantiated by any evidence.
9. There is no recovery or use of any ATM card by the applicant.
10. There is no medical report to corroborate the prosecution story.
11. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
12. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 04.07.2024 and is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE/INFORMANT:
13.
The bail application has been opposed on the ground that the victim was minor at the time of offence.

CONCLUSION:
14.
?The Supreme Court in Sushil Kumar vs. Rakesh Kumar, (2003) 8 SCC 673 has stated that it is more often in the Indian Society that person shows the age of their wards much below than their actual age.

entities.text: Sushil Kumar vs. Rakesh Kumar, (2003) 8 SCC 673
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also settled by Supreme Court that as per the medical records, a leverage of two years may be granted to the accused person.

In the case of Brij Mohan Singh vs. Priya Brat Narain Abhinav Pratap Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144241814/
2 Sinha, AIR 1965 SC 282, this Court, inter alia, observed that in actual life it often happens that persons give false age of the boy at the time of his admission to a school so that later in life he would have an advantage when seeking public service for which a minimum age for eligibility is often prescribed.

entities.text: Brij Mohan Singh vs. Priya Brat Narain Abhinav Pratap Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

16. ?A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
17.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ?Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
18. ?Learned A.G.A. could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
19. ?It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned A.G.A.
20.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

The bail application is allowed.
21. Let the applicant-Abhinav Pratap Singh involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance Abhinav Pratap Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144241814/
3 with law.
22.

entities.text: Abhinav Pratap Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

23. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
